publish_tests.label: Citability
publish_tests.statement: The item carries a stable identifier or locator and a stated version or date, so a citation made today names the same object tomorrow.

publish_tests.label: Quality control
publish_tests.statement: The item has passed the checks this wiki applies to it (sources cited and verified, contradictions flagged in place) and the check state is on the record, not assumed.

publish_tests.label: Ethical reuse
publish_tests.statement: The item's reuse terms are stated and respected: sensitivity class, consent and rights in its sources, and attribution are all honoured by the act of publishing it.

states.label: Share — made available to a named audience
states.statement: The page or dataset is made available to a named audience, as it stands. Sharing asserts availability only: the item may still change, and no citability, quality-control or ethical-reuse test is claimed for it. A shared item is not a published item, however wide the audience.

states.label: Publish — shared, and passing the three tests
states.statement: The page or dataset is made available AND passes all three tests stated in this vocabulary: citability, quality control, and ethical reuse. An item that fails any one of the three is shared, not published, whatever it is called.

states.label: Cite-ready — published, with a complete citation form
states.statement: The page or dataset is published AND carries a complete citation form on its face — identifier, version or date, and locator — that resolves as written, so another record can cite it exactly, without reconstruction. Cite-ready is a state of the citation form, not a stronger quality claim than publish.

vocabulary: Share / publish / cite-ready publication states (Marathon R13 lane BA; pattern: Kuusniemi & Nykyri 2025, LIBER Quarterly 35, Helsinki / Tampere, CC BY 4.0 — the distinction and its three publish tests only, restated in our own words). States are this wiki's own controlled vocabulary, held as data here and stated on wiki/rules/share-publish-cite-ready.md. A page may declare its state with the frontmatter field named in 'field'; an undeclared page has no state — undeclared is never read as published.
